content.text: After a parameter is edited in the results header, the Homes results page refreshes to the updated query without returning to the homepage.

expected_answer.baseline: Homes results page showing the pre-edit search parameters
expected_answer.operand: Homes results page updated to the edited parameters without homepage navigation

content.text: The results header allows direct editing of destination, dates, and guest parameters.

expected_answer.operand: results-header controls for destination, dates, and guests accept parameter edits on the results page

content.text: Each search parameter applied to the current Homes results query is visible in the results header.

expected_answer.operand: applied destination, date, and guest parameters are shown in the results header

judgements.rationale: [risk_factors] Applied risk factors: user-reach and change-frequency. This feature affects the core guest search journey on the Homes results page, so failures would broadly affect guests trying to refine a search in place. I did not apply money, auth, or data-loss because the cited scope is search routing and refinement only, with checkout/pricing changes explicitly out of scope and no authenticated or durable-data behavior stated.
